A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, table, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical characterizations and proofs. Empirical findings are attributed to other work; no original experiments or data analyses are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains purely theoretical. Its additional empirical observations come from cited studies, and its Limitations section explicitly leaves empirical comparison to future work.

M1.justification: The transformer model, restricted B-RASP operations, and constructive translations are retained. New Section 2 explains precision, masking, and positional-encoding restrictions already stated in v1, including Appendix D.1.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or tasks experimentally. V2's added flip-flop and language-hierarchy discussions concern theoretical implications and cited studies, not newly evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Neither version conducts baseline experiments. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparison classes; additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental evaluation protocols. Section 2 clarifies existing mathematical modeling assumptions without introducing training budgets, evaluation metrics, or testing procedures.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, or empirical supplementary analyses are added or removed. The new flip-flop explanation is a conceptual interpretation, not a conducted case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: No original empirical outcomes or performance values are added or revised. Table 1 preserves the same equivalences after terminology and reference updates.

T1.justification: Theorems B.1 and B.2 now require the minimal accepting DFA, correcting the scope of the automata–monoid equivalences. The principal equivalence theorems and constructive proofs in Appendices C–E remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged. Both versions retain the expressivity separation between leftmost and rightmost attention, the equivalence to the past-only LTL fragment and soft attention, and the direct logical and automata descriptions.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 adds a proposed explanation for flip-flop difficulties, and Section 8 connects the results to dot-depth and until hierarchies. Limitations newly discusses discrete attention as an obstacle to training and simulation using soft attention. These extend the retained interpretation.

D1.justification: The formal construction details in Appendix D are retained. Neither version supplies implementation instructions, experimental hyperparameters, hardware information, or code/data access for this work.

R1.justification: V2 adds Liu et al. (2023), Bhattamishra et al. (2020), three language-hierarchy references, and Yang et al. (2024b). These broaden the context while preserving the central positioning relative to Yang et al. (2024a) and Li and Cotterell (2025).

P1.justification: V2 adds Transformer Idealization as Section 2, subdivides the former Prologue into Separation, Characterizations, and Implications, and refines the B-RASP exposition and discussion. The overall argument sequence and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces its stacked output representation with a single updated vector and revises the caption to show residual addition, matching the existing text. Table 1 receives label and spacing changes, Figure 2 is relocated, and the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: V2 makes the modeling assumptions easier to locate, improves the introductory organization, and adds useful interpretive context. The minimal-DFA condition in Theorems B.1–B.2 improves mathematical precision, and Figure 1 becomes consistent with the residual-addition description. These are limited but supported improvements to an otherwise retained theoretical contribution.
